topic.title: Logical Operators
topic.description: Using AND, OR, and NOT operators

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Logical operators help you make decisions in code by combining or modifying conditions. Think of them as the 'and', 'or', and 'not' of programming!

• How to use AND (`&&`), OR (`||`), and NOT (`!`) operators
• Combining conditions to control program flow
• Avoiding common mistakes with logical operators

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a coffee shop deciding what to order:
- **AND (`&&`)**: You want coffee **AND** a croissant (both must be true)
- **OR (`||`)**: You want coffee **OR** tea (either is fine)
- **NOT (`!`)**: You want **NOT** decaf (invert the condition)

Logical operators work the same way in code! They let you combine boolean conditions (true/false values) to make smarter decisions.

• **AND (`&&`)**: Both conditions must be true
  Example: `if (age > 18 && hasTicket)` - must be adult AND have ticket

• **OR (`||`)**: Either condition can be true
  Example: `if (isRaining || isCold)` - bring jacket if either is true

• **NOT (`!`)**: Flips true to false (and vice versa)
  Example: `if (!isEmpty)` - do something if NOT empty

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Logical Operators works:

steps.title: AND Operator (`&&`)
steps.description: Checks if BOTH conditions are true. If either is false, the whole thing is false.

steps.title: OR Operator (`||`)
steps.description: Checks if EITHER condition is true. Only false if both are false.

steps.title: NOT Operator (`!`)
steps.description: Flips the boolean value. True becomes false, false becomes true.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ `&&` (AND) needs BOTH conditions to be true
✓ `||` (OR) needs just ONE condition to be true
✓ Combine them for complex conditions: `if ((a > b) && !(c == d))`
✓ Short-circuiting: Java stops checking after first false in `&&` or first true in `||`

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use parentheses to group conditions clearly
donts: Don't forget `!` flips the entire condition
Don't write `if (x == true)` - just `if (x)` is cleaner
sections.protip: Use `!` to simplify negative conditions: `if (!(age < 18))` is the same as `if (age >= 18)`

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Logical Operators used in real apps?

examples.how: Check if username AND password match: `if (usernameCorrect && passwordCorrect)`
Show products that are in stock OR on sale: `if (inStock || onSale)`
Check if player has key AND is at door: `if (hasKey && atDoor)`

problem.description:
Write a program that checks if a student passes an exam. A student passes if:
1. They score 50+ on the test OR
2. They score 40+ AND have perfect attendance

Test with these values: score = 45, attendance = true
hints: Remember the order of operations - use parentheses!
Test with different values to verify
problem.explanation: The condition checks if EITHER the score is 50+ OR (score is 40+ AND attendance is perfect). Parentheses ensure the AND is evaluated first.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Logical operators combine boolean conditions to make decisions
📌 `&&` = AND, `||` = OR, `!` = NOT - remember these symbols!
📌 Practice combining conditions with parentheses for clarity
📌 Ready to use these in if-statements and loops next!
